duets.lead: Halfway, and {leader} is the one everybody else is trying to catch.
duets.co: Tough job, since every rival now studies the man ahead and hunts for cracks.

duets.lead: The interval arrives, and {trailer} is breathing down the front man's neck.
duets.co: Close enough to pounce if he drops off, and that is the whole plan from here.

duets.lead: We reach the turn of the campaign, and the summit is up for grabs.
duets.co: Nobody has nailed it down, so every patch of good form from now on will decide the owner.

duets.lead: At the centre of the run the standings look tight, and the neutrals are loving it.
duets.co: Tight is the best news for anyone watching, since the big moves are yet to come.

duets.lead: The finish line is already in sight, and the pacesetter can almost taste it.
duets.co: Tasting it is the easy bit; the trick is keeping the legs fresh for the final miles.

duets.lead: At the midway mark the gap is only {margin} points, and that is nothing at all.
duets.co: A gap that small can vanish in a single purple patch, so anyone down the list should not relax.

duets.lead: Here comes the mark of the campaign, and {trailer} has the look of a hungry hunter.
duets.co: Hungry is right: the hunter has studied the favourite and is waiting for the first wobble.

duets.lead: Half of the Showdown is gone, and it is still anybody's game.
duets.co: The heart of the run is where early advantages get eaten away, so no one can switch off.

duets.lead: The mood has swung all campaign, and everyone is afraid to call it.
duets.co: Swings are what a campaign does to people; the table settles only once results stop surprising.

duets.lead: The midpoint, and {leader} has built a little breathing room at the summit.
duets.co: Breathing room is handy now, but a bad spell of form can take it away fast.

duets.lead: Past the interval, and {trailer} is making all the right noises in the background.
duets.co: Noises in the background are what hunters do, and the man ahead would be foolish to ignore them.

duets.lead: The midway point gives us our sharpest picture yet of who is genuinely serious.
duets.co: A picture this sharp is still a snapshot, not a verdict, so do not frame it yet.

duets.lead: At the mark, the lead stands at {margin}, and the chase is very much alive.
duets.co: A lead of {margin} is fragile when the pursuer can claw it back in a hurry.

duets.lead: We are past the midpoint and {leader} is exactly where they wanted to be.
duets.co: Comfortable is a fine place to be, but leaders who get comfortable tend to drop points.

duets.lead: Here is the thick of it, and {trailer} sits on the shoulder of the summit.
duets.co: The shoulder is the most dangerous spot in the campaign, since a single lapse hands it over.

duets.lead: The centre of the run has arrived, and the chasers already sound like a title side.
duets.co: They sound like one because they play like one, and that is what should worry the favourite.

duets.lead: Halfway through, and the man out front has not put a foot wrong yet.
duets.co: Avoiding mistakes for this long is the hardest trick in the game, and it rarely lasts a full haul.

duets.lead: Midway, and the big favourite on everybody's lips is still {leader}.
duets.co: Being the favourite right now is just a headline; the true test is holding the form.

duets.lead: This is where the early nerves turn into real plans.
duets.co: Plans need a bit of luck, but mostly they need patience, and patience gets tested most on a long haul.

duets.lead: The chase has come round, and it now looks like a proper fight.
duets.co: A proper fight is exactly what this Showdown needed; a one-sided affair would have been dull.

duets.lead: Exactly half, and the gap between the first two is still {margin} points.
duets.co: Small gaps at the interval are where careless managers slip, and none is careless yet.

duets.lead: We are halfway through, and {trailer} has started to sniff {leader}'s heels.
duets.co: Sniffing heels is a short-lived job unless the pursuer closes the gap in the games to come.

duets.lead: Rumblings of a title race are finally audible in this Showdown.
duets.co: Noise is fine, but a race only starts when somebody puts their foot down and keeps it there.

duets.lead: At the turn, the summit has been warm for a long time.
duets.co: A warm seat at the top is comfortable, which is exactly why it is dangerous to sit in too long.

duets.lead: The heart of it is here, and the one out in front has earned every bit of attention.
duets.co: Attention is the price of being out in front, and they have paid it without complaint.

duets.lead: The mid-run whistle is about to go, and the chaser looks ready to strike.
duets.co: Ready to strike is one thing; striking needs the man ahead to slip, and that rarely happens.

duets.lead: This is the chapter where the story finally takes some shape.
duets.co: Shape is a generous word, but the outline is clear: a leader, a chaser and a long road ahead.

duets.lead: We are at the midpoint, and {leader} talks like someone who wants the trophy.
duets.co: Talk is cheap at this stage; the trophy goes only to whoever is standing at the end.

duets.lead: Hands have changed at the peak more often than anyone predicted.
duets.co: Changing hands that often is thrilling to watch, but it makes the final miles hard to call.

duets.lead: The breather has arrived, and {trailer} has quietly crept back into contention.
duets.co: Quiet pursuers are dangerous, since no one watches them until the table says otherwise.

duets.lead: The body language at the summit says they have seen the whole plan already.
duets.co: Seeing the plan is one thing; the real test is whether it survives the first bad patch.

duets.lead: At the midpoint {leader} leads by {margin}, and the chatter is getting louder.
duets.co: Chatter is free, but wise managers ignore it in the thick of things.

duets.lead: The tension is building nicely as the run reaches its peak.
duets.co: Nicely is a polite word; for the men at the wheel it is a sleepless way to spend the interval.

duets.lead: Nothing has really been decided, and the whole thing feels wide open.
duets.co: That is exactly the feeling you want at this stage, as it keeps everyone honest and hungry.

duets.lead: Look at the mark, and the one nobody is talking about is {trailer}.
duets.co: Being overlooked this early is useful, because the leaders have not yet noticed the threat.

duets.lead: Now we see who fears whom.
duets.co: Fear is healthy at this point, as it shows both sides know what is on the line.

duets.lead: Pulling clear is the dream, and {leader} has broken away from the chasing pack.
duets.co: A lead this thin can be walked back, however good it feels.

duets.lead: Nothing is settled, and the picture is blurry after all this.
duets.co: A picture in progress is only a sketch, so it would be foolish to frame it yet.

duets.lead: So far, {trailer} has been the surprise of the whole campaign.
duets.co: Surprises are wonderful at this point, but they only count if they keep coming in the final stretch.

duets.lead: The middle is here, and {leader} has sent a real message.
duets.co: A message now is useful, but the chasing side has already read it and replied.

duets.lead: The form book is being torn up at the break.
duets.co: Torn up is strong; the form is shifting, and that is exactly what this stage should do.

duets.lead: The midpoint has landed, and the pressure is quietly moving to {leader}.
duets.co: Pressure moves when the pursuer closes in, and it can swing straight round if the favourite wobbles.

duets.lead: The table says the same thing to everyone: no one can relax yet.
duets.co: A shared warning is useful, since the top spot can change hands in the blink of an eye.

duets.lead: Even now, the chaser still believes the title is within reach.
duets.co: Belief costs nothing, but a chaser who keeps it never runs dry.

duets.lead: Every point from here carries more weight than the last, and everybody knows it.
duets.co: Points count for more as the season goes on, so the last few are the ones that will sting.

duets.lead: Time is ticking, and the favourite sits top of the form guide.
duets.co: Top of the guide is a fine seat, but guides get rewritten in the final stretch.

duets.lead: Setbacks have come and gone, and {trailer} has learned from each of them.
duets.co: Learning from setbacks separates a chaser from a champion, and this one is learning fast.

duets.lead: We are in the middle, and the lead has changed hands a few times.
duets.co: Few changes at the top so far, but it also means nothing is locked in yet.

duets.lead: Grinning at the break, {leader} looks like someone who knows something.
duets.co: Grinning is fine, but the actual knowledge only arrives when the last season is in the books.

duets.lead: Plenty of road still left, and the last word on this Showdown is far off.
duets.co: A long way off, but the road shortens every time someone takes the lead or loses it.
